raw_plan.interpretation: Treat this as a single-email acquisition campaign for a new, solution-aware buyer: a cost-sensitive ecommerce support team comparing alternatives to Intercom or Zendesk. The email should introduce Crisp through one concrete workflow—website chat handled in an omnichannel inbox—and ask the reader to start the 14-day all-features trial as the only next step.

intent.reason_now: The reader is evaluating customer-support platforms and may be sensitive to rising or per-seat costs, but their current provider and circumstances are unconfirmed.
intent.desired_action: Start Crisp's 14-day trial, install the chat widget on the store site, and test handling customer conversations in the omnichannel inbox.

raw_plan.reader: A solution-aware ecommerce support buyer comparing customer-support platforms and looking for a manageable way to handle website chat and other inbound conversations without committing before testing the workflow.
raw_plan.reader_segment: Cost-sensitive ecommerce support team replacing Intercom/Zendesk
raw_plan.reader_scope: Small ecommerce support teams within the selected segment that want to evaluate a website chat widget and omnichannel support inbox. Do not generalize product fit to every ecommerce business or assume the recipient currently uses a named competitor.
raw_plan.promise: Crisp gives an ecommerce support team website chat and one omnichannel inbox for customer conversations, with a 14-day all-features trial that requires no card before the team decides whether it fits.
raw_plan.orientation: Crisp is a customer support platform that provides a website chat widget and a single omnichannel inbox where a store's team handles customer conversations.
raw_plan.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognizing Crisp as another support-platform option to understanding the specific store workflow it enables and seeing a low-commitment way to test that workflow.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: One email is sufficient because the request explicitly requires one introduction and one next step. Lead with the operational value—website chat plus an omnichannel inbox—because that gives the reader a concrete reason to want Crisp. Use the flat-price Paid plan for up to 20 users as relevant commercial context without claiming savings, then make the 14-day all-features, no-card trial the single action. This order gives a solution-aware buyer the product, its useful operation, and the evaluation path without turning the email into a feature catalogue or unsupported competitor comparison. No separate objection or migration email is warranted, and the unsupported inbox-friction problem is excluded. Can this source be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

Qualified scope of the selected audience: Introduce Crisp as a website chat widget plus one omnichannel support inbox and invite the buyer to run it on their own site during the 14-day free trial, which includes all Crisp features and requires no card, as the single next step.. readers.what_it_sells: Crisp offers a website chat widget connected to one shared support inbox, which could let my team handle chat and other customer conversations in one place.
readers.biggest_doubt: For a cost-sensitive replacement decision, “flat pricing” is not enough: I still do not know the paid plan's actual price, so I cannot tell whether testing and installing it is worth the effort.
readers.stopped_at: If the workflow fits, a Crisp Paid plan offers flat pricing for up to 20 users.
fixes: Rewrite “If the workflow fits, a Crisp Paid plan offers flat pricing for up to 20 users.” as “After the trial, the relevant paid plan costs [exact amount and billing period] for up to 20 users.”
Rewrite “alongside other support conversations” to name the specific conversation channels included, so I can tell whether this could replace my current workflow without guessing.
Rewrite “Test it on your own site with a 14-day free trial.” to briefly state what installing the test requires and whether it can be removed without disrupting the existing support setup.

events.subject: A 14-day Crisp test
events.preview_text: Run website chat through an omnichannel inbox on your store, with no card required.
events.body:
Try Crisp on a real support task. Once its chat widget is installed on your store, customers can start website conversations that your team handles through Crisp’s omnichannel support inbox.

Crisp is a customer support platform for website chat and customer conversations. Its inbox gives your team one workspace for this chat workflow alongside the other support conversations you choose to handle there.

The trial lasts **14 days**, includes all Crisp features, and requires no card. Test the widget and inbox on your own site before deciding whether the setup fits your team.

Your team can make that decision after seeing the workflow in practice.
